premises.text: The huge blood testing market is spread over thousands of applications
premises.evidence_span: The blood testing market is huge. It's about $90 billion. The big problem is that it's spread over thousands of applications

premises.text: Existing analyzers detect only a handful of indications and most customers cannot pay the cost of ownership
premises.evidence_span: These existing blood analyzers can only detect a handful of indications, and most customers can't really pay the cost of ownership in order to cover the tests that they need

premises.text: Eliminating the analyzer — a disposable device that hooks to a phone and returns results on screen — makes testing easier and more affordable
premises.evidence_span: It takes a drop of blood, and the device hooks up to your phone with a dongle, a USB-C dongle, and you get the results on the screen

premises.text: The device is simple and modular: no pumps, no valves, and applications change by swapping reagents in the filters
premises.evidence_span: It's simple. It doesn't have pumps. It doesn't have valves

premises.text: The first test is ALT/AST liver enzymes, complementing blood gas analyzer menus and measurable only spectrophotometrically
premises.evidence_span: they complement the existing menus of blood gas analyzers, but they could only be measured spectrophotometrically

premises.text: Emergency veterinarians are the beachhead, running rapid screens for anesthesia or drugs before admitting patients
premises.evidence_span: we're launching this into the veterinary space, where emergency veterinarians could use it to run rapid screens for anesthesia or drugs before they admit the patients

premises.text: UC Davis validation across 100 animal samples and five species achieved R-squared 0.97 for ALT and 0.99 for AST
premises.evidence_span: We ran 100 animal samples across five different species, and we achieved an R-squared of 0.97 for ALT and a 0.99 for AST

premises.text: The rapid chemistry segment beyond liver has no low-cost competitors and no barriers to entry, inviting menu expansion
premises.evidence_span: it has no low-cost competitors. It has only about 20 analytes that are all generic

premises.text: Disruption comes from changing the model from razor-razorblade to a single-use disposable, with vertical integration controlling costs
premises.evidence_span: we are going to disrupt it by changing the model from a razor razor blade to a single-use disposable

value.text: Blood testing made easier and more affordable at the point of care
value.evidence_span: InDiagnostics is making testing easier and more affordable

notes: The problem framing is split into market fragmentation (P1) and analyzer inadequacy (P2) because they could fail separately: the market could stay fragmented while affordable broad-menu analyzers emerged, and vice versa. Device feature details (self-heating, sample-type flexibility, cuvette optics, microchip, two spare cuvettes) are folded into P3/P4 per v1.3.2 clarification 5. P5->P6 rests on the explicit 'the reason ... is because' warrant. Home-monitoring and research segments are folded into the expansion narrative rather than coded as separate premises. Market-size figures stay inside premises as quantitative detail.
